1 package org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.function.owner; 2 3 import org.springframework.samples.petclinic.model.Owner; 4 5 /** 6 * Single source of truth for an owner's {@code identityKey}: the one derived value that all 7 * create-time duplicate detection for {@code POST /owners} is expressed through. It consolidates 8 * what used to be several separate guards (telephone, email and household) into a single key, so a 9 * request is a duplicate only when its whole key equals an existing owner's. 10 * 11 *

The key is the lower-case hex SHA-256 of {@code normalizedTelephone + '|' + lowerEmail + '|' + 12 * soundex(lastName)}: 13 *

    14 *
  • telephone is canonicalised to E.164 ({@link OwnerTelephone#toE164OrRaw(String)}) so the 15 * comparison is independent of how a value happens to be formatted;
    • 16 *
  • email is the stored lower-cased form ({@link OwnerEmail#normalize(String)}) when present, 17 * otherwise the empty string (email is optional);
    • 18 *
  • last name contributes its Soundex code ({@link OwnerSoundex#of(String)}), so surnames that 19 * sound alike share that component.
    • 20 *
21 * 22 *

Because the telephone is part of the key, two owners with the same last name and postcode but 23 * different telephones have different keys and are both allowed (the later pipeline flags the second 24 * as a possible duplicate, see {@link AssignPossibleDuplicate}); only an exact full-key 25 * match counts as a duplicate. 26 * 27 *

Centralised here so {@link CheckOwnerIdentityUnique} (which rejects collisions) and the owner 28 * mapper (which returns the key) cannot disagree on how it is derived. 29 */ 30 public final class OwnerIdentity { 31 32 private OwnerIdentity() { 33 } 34 35 /** The identity key of an existing owner, derived from its stored fields. */ 36 public static String of(Owner owner) { 37 return key(owner.getTelephone(), owner.getEmail(), owner.getLastName()); 38 } 39 40 /** 41 * The identity key for the given parts: the lower-case hex SHA-256 of 42 * {@code normalizedTelephone + '|' + lowerEmail + '|' + soundex(lastName)}. 43 */ 44 public static String key(String telephone, String email, String lastName) { 45 String raw = OwnerTelephone.toE164OrRaw(telephone) + "|" + normalizeEmail(email) + "|" 46 + OwnerSoundex.of(lastName); 47 return Sha256.hex(raw); 48 } 49 50 private static String normalizeEmail(String email) { 51 return OwnerEmail.isPresent(email) ? OwnerEmail.normalize(email) : ""; 52 } 53 } 54

Done. The build is green.

## Summary

I implemented the structured owner-created event emitted via the `AUDIT` logger alongside the existing audit line.

**New file — `OwnerCreatedEvent.java`**: an immutable `record` with fields `seq`, `ownerId`, `customerCode`, `membershipLevel`, plus the constant `EVENT = "OWNER_CREATED"`. Its `toJson()` serializes the canonical `{seq, ownerId, customerCode, membershipLevel, event:'OWNER_CREATED'}` object (with proper JSON string escaping), built directly so the audit side-effect carries no dependency on the HTTP response serialization.

**`AuditOwnerCreated.java`**: after logging the human-readable line, it now constructs and logs the event as JSON. `seq` comes from a `static AtomicLong` incremented per create, so it's monotonically increasing across all creates and function instances.
